chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

A man who forgot the Tawaf al-Nisa' (the final circumambulation) until he reached Kufa, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Women are not permissible to him until he circumambulates the House.' I said: 'If he is unable?' He said: 'He should order someone to circumambulate on his behalf.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Then he should return to Mina and not spend the nights of Tashriq except in Mina; if he spends a night elsewhere, upon him is the blood of a sheep (dam). [He must be there] at dawn, unless he is in Mina. And if he departs after mid-night or at dawn, there is no harm upon him if dawn breaks while he is in Mecca.' And that which indicates that a blood offering is obligatory upon him if he spends every night in Mecca is what he narrated:

key_terms.اَلْكُوفَةَ: Kufa, a city in Iraq, indicating a significant distance from Mecca
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: Dam, a sacrificial offering of a sheep
key_terms.طَوَافَ اَلنِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa', the final circumambulation of the Kaaba that completes the Hajj
key_terms.لَيَالِيَ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ: The nights of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets Tawaf al-Nisa' before leaving Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the prohibition on marital relations for a pilgrim who forgets Tawaf al-Nisa' persists until the circumambulation is completed, either personally or via proxy. It further establishes the obligation to remain in Mina during the nights of Tashriq, prescribing a sacrificial penalty (dam) for those who stay in Mecca, while allowing flexibility for departure after dawn if one has already spent the night in Mina.
